name: Zinc

discovery.discoverer: Known in ancient India/China; isolated in Europe by Andreas Sigismund Marggraf, 1746

occurrence: Mined mainly from sphalerite (zinc sulfide) ore.
biologicalRelevance: An essential trace nutrient involved in immune function, wound healing, and as a structural cofactor in 'zinc finger' proteins that regulate gene expression.
notableCharacteristics: Technically borderline as a 'transition metal' since its d-subshell is completely full in both the metal and its common +2 ion — it forms no coloured compounds or variable oxidation states the way true transition metals do.
ncertRelevance: debate over whether Zn/Cd/Hg count as true transition elements
whyHere: With a fully filled 3d¹⁰ subshell in both its atom and its Zn²⁺ ion, zinc lacks the partially-filled d-orbitals that give true transition metals their colour and variable valency — which is exactly why some classifications leave it out of that group.
didYouKnow: Zinc coatings (galvanization) protect steel even when scratched, because zinc corrodes preferentially and sacrifices itself before the iron underneath starts rusting.
genZNote: Technically a transition metal, vibes like a main-group element. The identity crisis of the d-block.
